criteria.note: Generic runner ships at plugin/templates/scripts/runners/perf/warp_perf_runner.py. Read a journey (name, workload + workload_args, requests, concurrency, budgets), drives the workload across ThreadPoolExecutor worker threads, measures per-request latency and errored-ness, computes p50/p95/p99/max, throughput and error rate, exits 0 when budgets hold and 1 with each breach named. Independently confirmed the workload is a real seam: run(journey, workload=my_callable) invoked MY callable exactly once per request index 0..29 (the journey named the flaky built-in but zero errors resulted, proving the built-in was NOT used). Concurrency is real: a 40-request/8-concurrency sleep workload ran across 8 distinct thread ids with wall-clock 0.101s vs serial sum 0.800s, and every request index executed.

Budgets fail loud and pass when held. Drove check_budgets with known stats: max_p50/p95/p99 each fail naming the measured value (0.1000s / 0.2500s / 0.4000s); min_throughput_rps fails naming the measured rate (42.00 rps); max_error_rate fails naming the measured rate AND the failed count (0.200, 8/40). Each PASSES when the budget holds and at the exact boundary (strict > / < comparison), so it is not always-fail. Adversarial flatter probe (fast raising even-index requests + slow 20ms odd-index successes): raising requests were counted as errors (10 errors) and their latency EXCLUDED from the success percentiles (p50=0.0201s reflects only the slow successes, not the fast failures). Unknown workload fails loud (exit 1, ERROR message) rather than passing silently.

Both fixtures ship under plugin/templates/scripts/runners/perf/fixtures/. pass.journey.json (sleep 2ms, concurrency 8, generous latency + throughput budgets, zero error budget) exits 0. fail.journey.json (flaky every_n=4, zero error budget) exits 1 with 'max_error_rate: 0.250 exceeds budget 0.0 (10/40 requests failed)'. Determinism verified: ran fail fixture 8x (always exit 1, always 10/40) and pass fixture 8x (always exit 0). Confirmed the flaky built-in raises exactly on i%4==0 -> indices [0,4,...,36] = 10/40, index-chosen and timing-independent.

Control logic unit-tested in scripts/selftest.py with no external dependency: percentile over known arrays (empty->0, single, p50 of 1..9 = 5, p100 = max), summarize (error_rate, throughput excludes errors, ok/error counts), check_budgets met and exceeded for each budget kind, the runner driven over both shipped fixtures, a concurrency check that all 25 requests over 5 workers ran, and an unknown-workload-fails-loud case. Ran python3 scripts/selftest.py: 236 passed, 0 failed (16 perf expect() cases added; 220 + 16 = 236, internally consistent). ./scripts/verify.sh prints GATE: GREEN bound to 8ca8d4f.

Case-insensitive grep of the runner, both fixtures, wrapper, and README for bcengi/dejitech/travelpass/workpass/agentpass/coreconnect/onesim/mvne/dmitry/tripdesk/daybook/stripe/hubspot/ava returned zero matches; all added files are pure ASCII with no em-dash (U+2014), en-dash (U+2013), or double-hyphen. Both .warp/capabilities.yaml and plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml declare perf_load_runner status: reference (NOT mechanical) and are byte-identical (identical sha256 9668c5cb..., cmp identical). verify.sh docs-hygiene, secret, and template-sync gates all pass, GATE GREEN.

summary: Independently reran WARP-0304 end to end at HEAD 8ca8d4f (confirmed == the reviewed commit). Drove the runner over both fixtures via its CLI (pass exit 0; fail exit 1 naming 'max_error_rate: 0.250 exceeds budget 0.0 (10/40 requests failed)'), ran scripts/selftest.py (236 passed, 0 failed) and ./scripts/verify.sh (GATE: GREEN bound to 8ca8d4f). Adversarially I tried to break every claim without touching repo files: a flatter-latency probe (fast raising requests + slow successes) proved raising requests are counted as errors and their latency is excluded from the success percentiles; each of the p50/p95/p99, throughput, and error-rate budgets fails loud naming the measured value (error rate also names the failed count) and passes when the budget holds including at the strict boundary; the workload is a genuine seam (my own callable invoked once per index, not the built-in) with real cross-thread concurrency (8 distinct threads, wall-clock far below serial sum); a rubber-stamp test on tampered /tmp copies (latency budget 0.0, absurd throughput floor, p99 0.0) each flipped the pass fixture to exit 1 naming that budget, proving it is not always-pass; and determinism held over 8 repeats of each fixture with the flaky built-in raising exactly on i%4==0. The genericity, byte-identical capabilities (both status: reference), and dash/ASCII sweeps are all clean. I recomputed the manifest proof_digest myself and it equals sha256:3b016a75dffe676a. All five acceptance criteria are confirmed with zero blocking findings; verdict pass.
